name: OG Analytics
author: onlygrow

sections.description:
1.7 KB script, loaded async · no impact on speed
(tested on a site with 250,000 visits/day)
Real time · who is on your site, where they come
from, which page they read and for how long.
 Feature                                    OG Lite   Typical
 ─────────────────────────────────────────  ───────   ───────
 Server time per visit                       ~2 ms   200–600 ms
 Zero external requests                        ✓         ✗
 No WP-Cron (stats never get stuck)            ✓         ✗
 Visitors online now, live                     ✓       paid/~
 Tracking script (gzip)                      1.7 KB  3–28 KB
 Works with any cache plugin & SPA             ✓         ~

Know what’s happening on your site, right now. OG Analytics shows you who is visiting, where they came from and what they read — the second it happens — so you can see what works and do more of it. No Google account, no cookies, nothing sent to anyone: everything lives in your own WordPress.

Visits: page views · sessions · unique and first-time visitors · time on site · bounce rate · sources and channels · UTM campaigns · devices · browsers · countries and cities.

Dashboard: visitors online right now · visits chart · key numbers · top pages, sources and devices · world map · Visitors, Pages and Entry pages reports.

Inside WordPress: “Views” column in your posts and pages · views in the admin bar · chart in the post editor and on the WordPress dashboard.

Privacy: no cookies · IP addresses anonymized · data stays on your site · referrer spam and bots kept out · ghost mode against ad blockers.
sections.faq:
Does it use any external service?

Only to show countries and cities: it downloads the free IP to City Lite database by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com) once after activation and then monthly, and reads it on your own server, so no IP address is sent anywhere. License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — IP Geolocation by DB-IP. Terms and privacy: https://db-ip.com/legal

To show the icon of the websites that send you visitors, once a day (at your site’s quietest hour) it downloads the favicon of up to 100 of those websites directly from each one, and keeps it on your own server. Only the website’s address is used: nothing about your visitors is sent. Well-known sources (Google, Facebook, ChatGPT…) use icons included in the plugin. To turn it off, add add_filter( 'onlygrow_analytics_fetch_favicons', '__return_false' ); to your theme’s functions.php.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

It stays, so it comes back if you reinstall. To remove everything, turn on “Delete all data when the plugin is uninstalled” in Settings → Data.
sections.changelog:
0.2.12

  • [[new]] Settings → Exclusions: a daily limit of page views per visitor (300 by default). Whoever goes over it is a bot, and that whole day is left out of your numbers.
  • [[new]] Bots disguised as a normal browser are recognized by how their browser behaves (no screen, no languages, a fake Chrome…).
  • [[improved]] More bots recognized, including the ones that do not call themselves “bot” (GoogleOther, Google’s inspection tool, AI assistants, uptime monitors, security scanners).
  • [[improved]] Time on page counts only while someone is there: a tab left open with no activity stops adding time after 30 minutes, and coming back later starts a new visit.
  • [[improved]] More accurate countries: addresses sent with a port are understood, Cloudflare’s country is used when the location database does not know the address, and saved locations are refreshed with each new database.
  • [[improved]] Locations that no visit uses anymore are removed in the daily cleanup.
  • [[fixed]] Visitors on CUBOT phones were counted as bots.
  • [[fixed]] Right after an update, the first screen of the plugin could show “Route not found”.
  • [[fixed]] Form messages (a required field, “Drag to reorder”…) now follow your site’s language.

0.2.10

  • [[new]] The classic editor shows the chart of each post too, in a box on the side.
  • [[new]] Reports → Times: download each chart as CSV (by hour, by day of the week and the day × hour grid).
  • [[improved]] Works with WP Rocket and Autoptimize without excluding anything by hand: the tracking script is left as it is.
  • [[improved]] Clearer “View details” window: menu paths and notes are easier to read.
  • [[changed]] Pause tracking moved to Settings → Track.
  • [[changed]] The dashboard widget shows only visits, and a new icon for Tools.
  • [[fixed]] With WP Rocket’s “Delay JavaScript execution”, visitors who did not touch the page were not counted.
  • [[fixed]] After an update, the plugin screens could keep old styles until the browser cache was cleared.
  • [[fixed]] Tools → Diagnose no longer warns when an optimization plugin serves its own copy of the tracking script.
  • [[fixed]] The table in Tools → Diagnose no longer overflows its card.

0.2.09

  • [[new]] Paid AI channel: visits from ads inside ChatGPT are recognized.
  • [[new]] Websites that send you visitors show their own icon, downloaded once a day at your site’s quietest hour.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export with the same filters as the reports.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export: hourly totals.
  • [[improved]] Tools → Diagnose warns when a cache serves your pages with an old address of the tracker.
  • [[improved]] Smaller, lighter changelog labels.
  • [[fixed]] Ad clicks that arrive without a referrer (Google Ads on iPhone, Microsoft Ads, TikTok, LinkedIn…) were counted as Direct.
  • [[fixed]] Each ad click no longer shows up as a separate page.
  • [[fixed]] Cached pages keep counting after you turn ghost mode on or off.
  • [[fixed]] Reports work on hosts that limit large database queries.
  • [[fixed]] The “Every visit” export uses your site’s time zone.
  • [[changed]] Visit details are kept for 18 months; daily totals are kept forever.

0.2.08

  • [[new]] Every report has its own layout: Visitors, Geo, Devices, Pages, Entry pages and Sources.
  • [[new]] Content report: views by category, tag, your own taxonomies and author. Click a row to filter the whole report.
  • [[new]] Times report: when your visitors arrive, by hour, by day of the week and on a day × hour grid.
  • [[new]] Visitor journey: click the time of any visit to see that visitor’s visits and pages, in order.
  • [[new]] Download any table as CSV, choosing the columns, and print any report to PDF.
  • [[new]] Growth per row: how much each page, source or country grew against the previous period.
  • [[new]] New filters: site search (what people searched on your site) and continent.
  • [[new]] From Content, see the visits of a category, tag or author in one click.
  • [[new]] Tools → Diagnose: everything that can stop your site from counting, with what to do and a report to copy for support.
  • [[new]] A notice on the Dashboard when visits stop arriving at an hour that usually has them.
  • [[new]] A log of the page views your exclusion rules discarded, by reason.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export / Import your settings, and Tools → Restore defaults.
  • [[new]] Pause tracking without deactivating the plugin, with a notice on the Dashboard.
  • [[new]] Visits from comment spammers are not counted (spam comments and Disallowed Comment Keys).
  • [[new]] The views counter can wait until a post reaches a number of views.
  • [[new]] Dashboard widget: a comparison with the previous period (today, yesterday, 7 and 30 days, 12 months).
  • [[improved]] Changelog labels with a cleaner outline style.
  • [[improved]] On wide screens, the Dashboard shows four cards next to the chart.
  • [[improved]] Unique visitors per month and the sources of each entry page are kept forever.
  • [[improved]] More bots detected: user agents that include a web address or an email.
  • [[security]] A visitor’s IP address can no longer be faked with a header. Cloudflare and server proxies are detected on their own.
  • [[fixed]] Tracking works with Cloudflare Rocket Loader.
  • [[fixed]] No more false “REST API blocked” notice when your login session expires.
  • [[changed]] Visit details are kept for 12 months; daily totals are kept forever.
  • [[changed]] A new menu icon.

0.2.07

  • [[changed]] Changelog with color labels.

0.2.06

  • New changelog styles.

0.2.05

  • Sort the Visitors, Pages and Entry pages tables by any number column.
  • Key numbers show the change against the previous period (↗ / ↘), with the details on hover.
  • Counts page changes on single-page apps (sites that switch pages without reloading).

0.2.04

  • Visitors online now, under the main chart: where they come from, the page they are on and their time on site, live.
  • A one-time question about your kind of site, to set up the plugin for you.

0.2.03

  • A simpler, cleaner dashboard and reports.

0.2.02

  • New dashboard: visits chart, key numbers, visitors online, and top pages, sources, devices and countries with a world map.
  • New reports: Visitors, Pages and Entry pages.
  • Inside WordPress: views in the admin bar, a chart in the block editor sidebar and on the WordPress dashboard.
  • Referrer spam and known bots are kept out of your numbers.
  • Ghost mode (on by default): the script and the address that receives visits use a neutral name, so ad blockers don’t stop them.
  • IP addresses are now anonymized by default. Addresses stored before are anonymized once, in the background (this cannot be undone).
  • New “AI Assistants” channel: visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot and others no longer count as Referral.
  • iPads and Android tablets are now counted as tablets (before: desktop and mobile).
  • The real screen size and pixel density of each device are recorded.
  • Campaigns (UTM) are kept forever, by source, medium, campaign, term and content.
  • A session is shared by all the tabs of the same browser.
  • A bounce is now a single-page visit of less than 10 seconds with no interaction.
  • Visits by logged-in users record which user it was.

0.2.01

  • New analytics engine: sessions, visitors, sources, campaigns, devices, events, bounce rate, daily totals and retention.
  • Events are queued and processed in batches.
